headline: nodestone fixes AI coding agents forgetting context between sessions with one command
summary: nodestone is a new open-source project context memory engine that lives alongside your repo. It creates a compressed context pack, allowing AI agents to pick up exactly where they left off.
details: Developers often spend 20 minutes rebuilding context every time they open a new AI coding session, losing architectural decisions, unfinished tasks, and rationale for code snippets.

nodestone, a new open-source project, aims to solve this by acting as a project context memory engine. It lives alongside your repository, remembering crucial information across AI sessions and agents.

The tool creates a compressed context pack, typically around 500 tokens, which captures active tasks, recent decisions, detected drift between plans and code, and milestone status. This pack is then provided to your AI agent as system context.

Unlike per-chatbot memory solutions, nodestone is per-project, ensuring context follows the repository rather than being tied to a specific chat window. It is designed to work across various AI agents, including Claude, Cursor, and Gemini.

nodestone also features drift detection, comparing actual file changes against your project plan. This helps identify discrepancies and ensures your AI agent understands why changes occurred and what the next steps should be.
The project is free and open-source, available for installation via `pip install nodestone`. Developers can find more information and contribute on deepstrain.dev or its GitHub repository.

headline: Israeli firm BlackCore suspected of meddling in votes in New York and Scotland
summary: Israeli firm BlackCore is under scrutiny for alleged interference in democratic processes in New York and Scotland, raising significant concerns about election integrity.
details: Israeli cybersecurity firm BlackCore is reportedly under suspicion for involvement in vote meddling. The allegations point to activities impacting elections in both New York and Scotland.
These suspicions, emerging from a Hacker News report, highlight potential attempts to influence democratic outcomes. The specific nature of the alleged meddling has not been fully detailed.

The case brings to light critical questions about the role of private security firms in national and local elections. It underscores the ongoing challenges in safeguarding electoral systems from external interference.
Authorities are expected to investigate these claims thoroughly to ascertain their veracity. The outcome could have significant implications for cybersecurity regulations and international relations.
